ground_truth.unit: log points of annualised household electricity consumption (kWh)
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Effect of the Reform on Residential Electricity Consumption and Expenditure (2011-2014)"), column (1), row Reform (T): the paper's difference-in-differences estimate of the August 2013 Spanish electricity pricing reform (fixed charge raised, regulated volumetric rate cut) on household electricity consumption, estimated by OLS.  Data: Spanish Household Budget Survey households interviewed between August 2011 and April 2014, each interviewed twice, in the same two-week period of two consecutive years; the control group has both interviews before the reform, the treated group its second interview after it.  T is the post-reform dummy for interviews whose electricity bill falls under the reform (the paper places the response one month after the reform, when households receive a reformed bill).  Dependent variable: log of electricity consumption in the month before the interview (kWh, annualised by the survey).  Regressors: T, log household price per kWh (expenditure divided by consumption), log income and its square, months since reform, and controls for household size, number of rooms, dwelling surface, elderly members, education of the household head, household economic situation (number of economically active members), renting, building older than 25 years, municipality-size dummies, urban area, province capital, regional dummies, quarterly dummies and year fixed effects.  No household fixed effects.  Standard errors clustered at the household level.

i4r.notes: Team 49 blanket verdict (code reproduces the paper's output); no meta-database row for column 1.

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=-0.11934 vs claimed=-0.178 (relative error 32.96%, tolerance 15.17%, the ±1·SE band with SE=0.027).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Price, income and instruments taken in the dataset's CPI-deflated form (lnPRE, lny/lny2, lnPRE_papas_/lnPRE_aguav_/lnPRE_gascar_); the paper does not state whether prices are deflated. Income is only available deflated, so the price was kept in the same real terms.
Instruments use the dataset's imputed versions (missing household prices replaced by the period mean), so OLS and IV columns share one sample, as Table 2 reports identical N in all columns.
Retirement income (PENSIO_j) is not included as a control: it is in Table 1 but not in the control list of equation (4).

LIML implemented by hand (k-class with kappa = minimum eigenvalue); household-FE LIML estimated on within-demeaned data (FWL). Only point estimates are scored; cluster-robust SEs are printed as diagnostics.

Number of id counts all households in the estimation sample, including 586 that are left with a single observation after listwise deletion (fixest drops them from the FE fit; they do not affect the coefficients).
cell.notes: Data: analysis data/data_to_run_DOFILE3.dta (read with haven). Sample: observations with the reform dummy T2 defined (Sept 2011-Mar 2014 interviews; 25,775 obs / 12,888 households, matching the paper's panel size), then listwise deletion on regression variables (mainly economic-situation missing for 4,445 obs and surface for 462) -> 20,872 obs, 10,729 households. Dependent variables lnc_ele and lng_ele (log annualised kWh and EUR). Regressors: T2, log real kWh price, log real income and its square, months since reform (dist), household size, rooms, m2, elderly, renting, building >25 yrs, urban, province capital, education (4), economic situation (3), municipality size (5), region (CCAA), quarter dummies, year dummies; household FE in cols 3/4/7/8; SEs clustered by household. Three exploratory runs (variable listing, tabulations, variable-definition checks) printed no RESULT lines. No author scripts or result files were opened.
